title: Refactor emission state machine and priority lanes to reduce streaming TTFB
author: Anjali Rao
release_notes: Reduce first-byte latency for streaming generation by introducing an explicit emission state machine, priority lanes for low-latency streams, and soft-credit backpressure. Includes observability hooks and regression tests. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context & motivation: Customers running low-latency chat/assistants observed tail and first-byte spikes under mixed workloads where long-running batch streams interfered with interactive requests. This PR introduces an emission-focused state machine and per-stream priority lanes to ensure interactive streams get earlier kernel dispatch and opportunistic KV prefetching. The goal is to decrease median and P95 TTFB for streaming tokens without harming aggregate throughput.

Design summary: 1) EmissionState: replace ad-hoc token loop with a small deterministic state machine (Idle -> Ready -> Emitting -> Paused -> Finished). Transitions are driven by credits, kernel readiness, and a new priority hint on each stream. 2) Priority lanes: streams are tagged as high/normal/low; scheduler maintains lightweight queues and enforces a short head-of-line preemption window so high-priority streams can steal upcoming microbatch slots. 3) Soft-credit backpressure: credits are now virtual (soft) so low-priority streams yield proactively under congestion instead of being forcefully stalled, reducing contention bursts. 4) Opportunistic KV prefetch: small prefetch window for predicted next-token KV keys when a stream enters Ready; prefetch is limited by a budget to avoid noisy eviction patterns. 5) Observability: token-level timers for state transitions, per-lane queue depths, and prefetch hit/miss counters were added to aid tuning.

What changed (high-level files): runtime/emitter.h, runtime/emitter.cpp (emission state machine + unit tests); runtime/scheduler.cpp (priority lanes and preemption window); runtime/kv_cache.cpp (budgeted prefetch + cache hints); runtime/continuous_batcher.cpp (minor integration to respect lanes); tests/streaming_latency_test.py (regression harness + synthetic mixed workload); docs/streaming-latency-notes.md (design rationale + tuning knobs); ci/flake8-rules.cfg (lint adjustments for new code). Small illustrative snippet (for reviewer context):

// state transition sketch
// Idle --(newRequest)-> Ready --(credits & kernel_ready)-> Emitting --(rate_limit)-> Paused --(resume)-> Emitting/Finished

Commits (summary):
- 0a1b2c3: Introduce EmissionState and basic loop replacement (emitter.*). Add unit tests for state transitions.
- 1d2e3f4: Scheduler priority lanes implementation and preemption window; integrate with continuous batcher.
- 2f3g4h5: KV prefetch budget implementation and observability counters; extend latency regression test scenarios.

Checklist: [x] Design doc linked in PR, [x] Unit + integration tests, [x] Metrics exposed for canary, [x] No semver-breaking API change, [x] Manual perf run (see notes below).

Performance results (local perf lab synthetic mixed workload, 8-GPU pool, baseline==main): Median streaming first-byte latency: 18ms -> 11ms (-39%). P95: 72ms -> 36ms (-50%). Overall tokens/sec throughput: -3% at extreme saturation (expected tradeoff); typical 10-20% tail improvements with negligible median throughput change. Results attached in CI artifacts and docs/streaming-latency-notes.md.

Testing & CI: Initial CI run: lint failed due to style in emitter tests (fixed in follow-up commit). Unit+integration tests: pass. Synthetic latency regression harness: included and green. Load runner noted minor increase in KV eviction under pathological synthetic low-memory test — we added prefetch budget to avoid regressions and document tuning.

Review conversation (high level):
- Marco Jensen: Suggested clearer invariants for Ready -> Emitting to avoid race with kernel handoffs. Asked for a stress test for rapid connect/disconnect. Action: added test covering 5000 short streams and explicit assertion for state cleanup.
- Priya Kapoor: Requested metrics for per-lane preemption counts and a flag to opt-out of priority lanes for Dedicated customers. Action: added per-lane counters and a runtime knob (enable_priority_lanes=false) that defaults to true.
- Ethan Cole: Raised concern about KV prefetch noise. Action: implemented budgeted prefetch and exposed prefetch_budget config; added hit/miss metrics.
- Author replies: Addressed all requested changes; included short tuning guide in docs/streaming-latency-notes.md.

Merge notes: After reviews and two CI reruns (lint fix + perf artifact inclusion), PR was approved by Marco and Priya and merged via squash on 2026-02-27. Commit message summarizes the state machine, priority lanes, soft-credit backpressure, and KV prefetch budget.

Operational guidance: For customers sensitive to throughput under extreme saturation, set enable_priority_lanes=false or tune prefetch_budget and preemption_window in runtime config. Default knobs are conservative and expected to help most interactive workloads.
notes_for_oncall: If streaming regressions are reported after deploy: 1) check metrics emitter.state_transition_errors and per-lane queue_depth; 2) verify prefetch_hit_rate is non-zero and prefetch_budget not exceeded; 3) if throughput drop, consider toggling enable_priority_lanes temporarily and engage perf team. Linked Linear items track follow-ups: ENG-7891 (observability follow-ups), ENG-8032 (tuning defaults).
